quotes.text: I am open to reforming the grocery sales tax, but I believe that we should first reform property tax.
quotes.editor_note: From a WKRN interview on affordability (WKRN's own page blocks automated fetches; text confirmed via a syndicated Yahoo News copy, wording is the publisher's direct quotation) where Rose was asked about cutting the grocery tax; he backs cuts but sequences property-tax reform first, a distinct prioritization from Fritts's grocery-tax-first pledge and Blackburn's spending-review-first answer. Dropped his preceding generic 'cut taxes anywhere I can' sentence as non-distinctive filler; this sentence reads complete on its own, so no ellipsis is needed.

quotes.text: We've got to have a governor who will work hard to make sure that our local law enforcement agencies have the support and the manpower they need.
quotes.editor_note: From the same WKRN interview, on how the state should fund and operate public safety; Rose frames the governor's role as ensuring local police departments get adequate staffing and resources, distinct from Fritts's National Guard critique in the same race. Verbatim, no edits.

quotes.text: The overwhelming majority of Tennesseans want parents to have options.
quotes.editor_note: From a WVLT sit-down interview alongside his two primary opponents (2026-07-23) on school choice; Rose backs continuing the Education Freedom Scholarship voucher program on parental-choice grounds, unlike Fritts who would cancel it. Verbatim, no edits.

quotes.text: We cannot allow Wall Street investment firms to buy up our housing supply [and] convert them to rentals.
quotes.editor_note: From Rose's written answer to the Nashville Banner's July 2026 candidate questionnaire on housing affordability — a campaign written statement (text, not video-verifiable), flagged as a lower-tier source. His fix targets corporate/institutional buyers rather than permitting rules, a different mechanism than Blackburn's deregulation-first answer in the same questionnaire. Bracketed '[and]' to join two reported clauses into one grammatical sentence; otherwise verbatim.
